explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: An API receives a request and returns data.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Imagine opening a product list. Who requests the products? Who stores them?

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: The browser asks; the API route responds; Supabase stores the products.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: fetch requests data. You also need to check whether the request succeeded.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: On your local site, open /api/products?active=true&limit=3 in the browser.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: You see JSON, not cards. The component turns that data into a display. An empty list can be valid.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: The route.ts file defines the response at an API address.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: In your test project, create app/api/hello/route.ts, copy the example, run npm run dev and open /api/hello.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: You should see message: Hello and ok: true. Replace Hello with Bonjour and reload to check your change.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: The HTTP status is a clue for finding an error.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Open a missing address in your local project, then compare it with /api/hello if you created it.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: 404 means not found. 200 means success. Note the address and status before investigating.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: Code, data and files have different roles.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Sort these three items: Header.tsx, a product price, its photo.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: Header.tsx → code; price → database row; photo → file in Storage.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A Supabase project is a space containing your database and its services.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: In a test Supabase project, find Table Editor, SQL Editor and Storage. Leave the real shop untouched.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: Table Editor shows rows; SQL Editor runs instructions; Storage holds files.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: RLS decides which rows a user can read or create.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Read the two SQL policies below. Find auth.uid() and user_id: why compare them?

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: The signed-in ID must match the note owner. To actually verify protection, test with two accounts through the app.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A bucket is a storage container with access rules.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Decide where to put a product photo and a private customer document.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: Public photo → public bucket. Customer document → private bucket with authorized access. Public does not mean anyone can upload.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A migration changes structure; a backup lets you restore data.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Write down what to back up before changing a table containing product photo references.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: Database rows and Storage files, separately. Reverting a deployment does not restore the database.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: Choose services based on your project’s actual needs.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: List three shop needs: related data, photos and website publishing.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: Supabase covers data and files; Vercel publishes the site; GitHub keeps code and its history.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: GitHub keeps your code. Vercel turns it into an accessible website.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: In a new test project, prepare the .gitignore below before staging files in Git.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: With git status --ignored, .env.local should be ignored. No secret should be staged for commit.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A commit is a local version. A push sends it to GitHub.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Run the commands one at a time in your new project. Pause at git diff --cached to review files.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: After pushing, GitHub shows your commit and expected files. The site is not deployed to Vercel yet.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: Vercel uses your repository and environment variables to build the site.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Import your test repository into Vercel. Check the package.json folder and add test variables before deploying.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: A successful deployment provides a URL. If the build fails, read the first error in its logs.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A working URL must also show the correct data.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: Open the deployment link on your phone. Check a page, an image and an API request before connecting a domain.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: The page fits the screen, the image loads and the API returns the expected data.

explanation.title: idea
explanation.text: A branch and preview let you check a change before publishing it.

explanation.title: task
explanation.text: In your test project, change a heading on a branch, push it and compare the Vercel preview with the published site.

explanation.title: result
explanation.text: The new heading appears in the preview. Check it before merging into the production branch.
